text: You're snowed inside a warehouse store with a stranger you caught, and someone outside is breaking in.
The bay door screams up another inch. Headlights spill through the gap.
"Who is that?" Dana snaps at Ray. "Who did you tell?"
"Nobody," Ray says. "I heard them in the lot before the storm. They want to empty this place while the roads are closed."
Through the gap, a yellow plow truck idles in the snow. Men in headlamps are digging.
"Barricade," Dana says. "Now."
Marcus fires up the forklift. You drag pallets of water against the door.
Then the keypad by the bay door beeps. Once. Twice.
Green light. Someone outside just typed Dana's alarm code.
Dana grabs Ray's notebook and flips to the back. The page with her code is torn out.
"I never took it," Ray says. "I swear."
The pallets start sliding. The door rises a foot. A gloved hand reaches under.
"Is there another way out?" you shout.
Ray looks up. "Roof hatch. Cut me loose."
Dana stares at him for one long second. Then she nods, and you cut his zip ties.
Ray climbs the racking in aisle twenty-two, and you all follow him into the dark.
Above the top shelf, there's a crawlspace only he knows. It runs right over the loading dock.
Below you, four men in headlamps squeeze under the bay door.
Ray pops the roof hatch. Snow pours in.
You slide down the drift to the dock, right next to their truck. It's still running.
You and Ray haul the bay door down. Dana wraps the plow's tow chain through the handles and snaps the lock.
Inside, fists hammer the door. They're trapped in the dock.
Then you notice Marcus isn't with you.
Through the crack under the door, you see his yellow vest. He's inside with them. Talking.
A torn notebook page sticks out of his vest pocket.
Dana's voice cracks. "Marcus had my code."
Ray stares at the door. "He's the one I saw in the lot."
By dawn, the snow stops. Red and blue lights flash at the top of the drift.
A county plow clears the lot, and three police cruisers roll in behind it.
They unchain the bay door. Four men come out in handcuffs. Then Marcus, who won't look at Dana.
An officer asks who caught them. Dana points at Ray. "He did."
Behind you, the front doors finally slide all the way open.
